summary: Most Hebrew words are built on a root of three consonants with a basic meaning; patterns of vowels and extra letters (for verbs the seven binyanim) make the actual words. Recognizing the root helps to read without vowels and to remember word families.

askYourself: Which consonants remain when I remove ה ו ב ל מ ש in front and the endings?
Are ו and י here letters of the root or only vowel letters?
Do I know another word with the same root?

traps: In full spelling ו and י often only show a vowel: in כּוֹתֵב the ו is not part of the root כ-ת-ב.

quiz.q: What is the root of כּוֹתֵב ‘writes’?
quiz.why: The ו only shows the vowel o.

quiz.q: Which word shares a root with מִכְתָּב ‘letter’?

quiz.why: There are seven; each gives the root a different shade of meaning.
